sampling_model.design: Superpopulation observational sampling with no parametric model for the categorical distribution, propensities, or outcome regressions.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment \(A\) with identification by consistency and conditional exchangeability given \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed \(\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass category.
sampling_model.outcome: Real outcomes with \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\) and explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth central moments at most \(M^4\); this implies conditional variances at most \(M^2\) but imposes no standardized-kurtosis or positive-variance condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pilot-selected saturated cells, a light-cell one-mark Chebyshev factorial lift, robust heavy-cell ratios, and cross-fitted saturated empirical nuisances for the local comparator.
sampling_model.computation: Exact categorical and treatment coordinates, dyadic enclosures of real outcomes and known scalars, recurrence evaluation of polynomial coefficients and factorial terms, outward interval arithmetic, and monotone bisection to requested endpoint accuracy \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\).
sampling_model.randomness: All probabilities and expectations are under the observed iid sample law \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds worst-case mean squared error for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\) by the order of \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) under fixed overlap; Appendix C.5 sets the control-arm regression to zero in the hard family.
The paper constructs heavy-light best-polynomial factorial-moment estimators attaining minimax mean squared error for additive discrete-distribution functionals.

Sections 4.1--4.2 develop scalar bounded-influence mean and variance score bounds under Catoni's stated moment and kurtosis conditions; they do not establish a uniform conditional raw fourth-central-moment envelope for a selected marked-factorial statistic.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds expected confidence length in Gaussian nonparametric experiments by a between-class modulus and the paper constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals.
Theorem 5.1 gives uniformly valid asymptotically efficient Gaussian ATE intervals from cross-fitted orthogonal scores under nuisance-rate conditions.

The Abstract and Sections 2--4 derive finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE estimators and confidence intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions when regression errors are normal with known variance, with feasible asymptotic extensions for unknown errors.
Theorem 3.1 gives a self-normalized moderate-deviation expansion for fixed-order nondegenerate Studentized U-statistics under moment conditions.
The paper gives nearly tight dimension-free confidence intervals for probabilities of individually unobserved multinomial events.

body.tldr: Unrestricted categorical adjustment creates two inferential regimes inside the same identified ATE model: a regular influence-function regime when every relevant cell is populated and a rare-cell regime in which unseen categories produce an additional \(d/[n\log(en)]\) uncertainty term. The project characterizes the minimax worst expected length of uniformly honest intervals over the global arbitrary-cell-mass class with an explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope as \(M\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\), imports the accepted real-mark heavy-light Chebyshev factorial estimator as approximation infrastructure, equips its selected rare-cell statistic with a new directly observable tail certificate derived from that raw envelope, gives a certified dyadic implementation with explicit endpoint tolerance and bit complexity, proves the matching lower bound directly from same-class confidence-length tests after an explicit control-arm-zero transfer of Zeng et al.'s one-arm source experiment, and shows on a separately imposed balanced local submodel with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\) that the robust interval's endpoints merge at \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) with the cross-fitted saturated-cell Gaussian interval.

project_justification.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, establishes the large-alphabet point-risk obstruction for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\), not directly for the ATE, and Section 6 warns that the 401(k) bootstrap and Gaussian intervals may miss nominal coverage. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 already supplies the real-mark heavy-light approximation and point-risk infrastructure, but not a directly observable tail radius. ArmstrongKolesar2021 provides finite-sample bias-aware ATE inference after imposing smoothness or shape restrictions and normal known-variance errors; it does not cover arbitrary categorical masses under fixed overlap and the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope. Catoni2012 supplies a scalar score template under its own assumptions, not a theorem for this raw conditional envelope or the selected marked-factorial statistic. Expected honest length is not determined by any of these point-risk results, and regular DML theory does not cover empty saturated cells.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is one interval for the unrestricted discrete model whose finite-sample calibration is proved directly from the absolute conditional fourth-moment envelope and acts on the banked selected marked-factorial statistic without standardized-kurtosis or positive-variance conditions, whose rational implementation has certified endpoint error, whose lower bound is proved as a coverage-to-testing statement in the identical global causal class after an explicit one-arm-to-ATE reduction, and whose local radius becomes the efficient Gaussian radius on a clearly separated regular submodel.
project_justification.fill: The accepted one-mark real-outcome Chebyshev factorial estimator supplies rare-cell approximation infrastructure; a compatibility lemma exposes its selected statistic without changing its bias guarantee; a bounded-influence exponential score, using Catoni only as a scalar algebraic template, supplies a data-only tail radius proved from the unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope; recurrence-based coefficient and factorial evaluation with outward interval arithmetic supplies a finite-precision certificate; a control-arm-zero scaling identity transfers the published \(\psi_1\) hard family to the ATE model before same-class ATE-separated testing priors supply the expected-length converse; and a Hajek-projection expansion on the separately imposed balanced local submodel connects the globally honest interval to the saturated one-step benchmark.

body.related_work: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 is the exact global-model anchor: its categorical class permits arbitrary and zero cell masses, its Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\), and Appendix C.5 implements the hard family with the control-arm regression set to zero. Proposition \(prop:zeng\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}to\text{-}ate\text{-}reduction\) records the scaling and subclass identity required before that rate can inform ATE lower bounds; the present same-class theorem must still construct ATE-separated prior supports and prove their total-variation bound. The paper's Appendix A.1 describes a saturated plug-in Gaussian regime, and Section 6 documents \(n=9915\), \(d=8196\) with uncertain interval coverage. The lower bound \(P_n(X=k)\ge c_0/d_n\) is not attributed to that paper; it is an explicit project-imposed restriction defining only the regular local submodel for linearization, variance consistency, and endpoint equivalence. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), is reusable infrastructure: it already constructs the clipped real-mark heavy-light Chebyshev factorial estimator and proves its risk order without an additional logarithmic factor. The compatibility lemma here only rewrites and rescales that estimator so the new directly observable tail score can act on its selected marked-factorial statistic. ArmstrongKolesar2021, Abstract and Sections 2--4, is the closest finite-sample honest-ATE comparator: it optimizes bias-aware intervals conditional on realized treatment and covariates under smoothness or shape restrictions, with exact finite-sample optimality for normal known-variance errors and feasible asymptotic extensions otherwise; the global class here instead has arbitrary categorical cell masses, fixed overlap, and an explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope, so its rare-cell frontier is not a smoothness-model corollary. JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015, Section 4, and WuYang2019 provide the polynomial and factorial-moment lineage of the banked estimator, not an additional novelty claim of this proposal. Catoni2012, Sections 4.1--4.2, supplies only a scalar bounded-influence exponential-score template under its own assumptions. It neither assumes nor proves this proposal's uniform conditional raw fourth-central-moment envelope, and it does not subsume the new selected-factorial calibration when conditional variances may vanish; the score inequalities here must be derived directly from the absolute \(M^4\) envelope. Low1997 and CaiLow2004 separate honest expected length from point loss through coverage-to-testing and modulus arguments; the present converse adapts that logic to fixed-sample causal prior mixtures rather than claiming their Gaussian theorem applies verbatim. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML, Theorem 5.1, and Hahn1998 give the efficient ATE influence-function benchmark; the local result establishes endpoint equivalence to that benchmark on the deliberately balanced submodel while the global theorem covers arbitrary-mass laws outside its nuisance-rate regime. ShaoZhou2016, Theorem 3.1, informs projection and studentization but assumes a fixed-order nondegenerate U-statistic. Painsky2022 gives large-alphabet intervals for individual unseen probabilities, whereas the target here is an overlap-coupled causal aggregate with real outcome marks.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The explicitly imposed conditional raw fourth-central-moment envelope implies the conditional variance bound \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid X=k,A=a]\le M^2\) by the conditional moment inequality, but it does not imply a uniform bound on conditional kurtosis when a cell variance approaches zero. Catoni2012 therefore cannot be invoked as a black-box theorem for this model: the observable calibration must derive its score bound from the absolute \(M^4\) envelope inside the marked-factorial construction without adding positive variance. The local Gaussian claim is restricted to nondegenerate efficient variance, but the global honesty claim is not.
body.honest_scope: The global theorem program fixes \(\epsilon\), \(M\), and \(\alpha\), allows arbitrary and zero cell masses and real outcome laws satisfying only the stated mean envelope and the explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope, and claims no adaptation to unknown \(M\) or shrinking overlap. The raw envelope implies a conditional variance upper bound but imposes neither standardized kurtosis nor positive conditional variance. Catoni2012 is used only as a scalar bounded-influence score template and is not cited as a source of this model condition or as a theorem covering the selected marked-factorial statistic. The balanced lower-mass condition is an explicitly imposed local regularity condition, not a property of the global class or an assumption attributed to ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024; it is used only for local linearization, variance consistency, endpoint equivalence, and the nondegenerate fixed-alphabet sanity check. The real-mark heavy-light Chebyshev factorial approximation is imported from CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 and is not claimed as new. The direct rare-cell calibration under the raw envelope, robust block constants, polynomial constants, critical-value computation, and same-class confidence-length testing priors are the principal solve outputs. Zeng et al.'s Theorem 2 enters only through its stated \(\psi_1\) target and the explicit control-arm-zero subclass reduction; no ATE interval lower bound is attributed directly to that theorem. Finite-precision evaluation uses dyadic enclosures and outward rounding, so it does not restrict the statistical law to rational outcomes. When efficient variance vanishes, only the stated unstudentized collapse is claimed.
